title: Research: lower bounds for small complex units: m = 2 never saves, m = 3 needs 14W/5 calls (Lean, engine game), m = 4 needs 41W/13, and the smallest open cases (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds one package, `research/complex-small-m-lower-bounds`. It collects lower bounds on the number of calls s that a
unit for W complex arrays needs at small block size m, each in a stated game, and the smallest shapes they leave
open. It is a bounded index of one obstruction family plus the bounds behind it. No construction, no new κ, no
claim about integer multiplication.

| Result | Game | Status |
|---|---|---|
| The kept-subspace bound (a general form of #288's FO lemma) | engine game | proved in Lean |
| m = 2: s ≥ 2W | engine game; every game with bounded free steps | proved in Lean; argued by hand in the bounded games (one AI reviewer) |
| m = 3: s ≥ 14W/5 (saving at most 6.28e-2; every unit with 4 or fewer arrays excluded) | engine game; widened game | proved in Lean; argued by hand in the widened game (three AI reviewers) |
| m = 4: s ≥ 41W/13 (saving at most 1.71e-1) | engine and widened games | checked by computer; in the widened game it also rests on the keptness argument, argued by hand |
| m ≥ 4: at least 2.9447 calls per array (2.99172 at m = 5, 2.97290 at m = 6) | engine game | argued by hand (two AI reviewers reproduced the numbers) |
| m = 3 without phase letters: s ≥ 3W for every group of address maps | no-phase game | argued by hand (one AI reviewer); certificate checked by computer here |
| One array needs m calls; W ≥ 2 arrays need max(W + m, 2W) | every game with bounded free steps | argued by hand (AI reviewers) |

The engine game is the game of the Lean engine in my repository: OpenAI's letters (calls C_v, shifts, rational
mixing with scratch) plus invertible XOR-linear address maps and phases i^(z·x + c). Every bound is for units right
at every number of digit columns. The Lean statements are for rational mixing; complex mixing is argued from the
same proof. Statuses use my public repository's words; no person has read any of the proofs.

Smallest open shapes (engine game): 5 in 14 at m = 3 (6.28e-2, exactly on the bound), 2 in 7 at m = 4 (9.63e-2),
3 in 10 and 4 in 13 at m = 4; 2 in 7 and 3 in 9 at m = 5; 2 in 8 and 3 in 9 at m = 6 (3 in 9 is not excluded by any
bound I know). In games that make neighbouring-column maps free, 2 in 5 and 3 in 6 at m = 3.

README section 7 answers the two small-gadget questions in David Harvey's note "On the recently proposed
o(n log n) integer multiplication algorithm" (20 October 2026): why one array cannot save (his §6; argued by hand, for programs right at every digit width), and his
suggested search for "a non-trivial gadget for I ⊗ B^(⊗3) acting on C^4 ⊗ (C^2)^(⊗3)" (his §8), which needs at
least 12 calls by the m = 3 bound (14 × 4 = 56 > 55 = 5 × 11): proved in Lean for C-calls with rational mixing,
argued by hand for complex mixing and B-calls, for programs right at every digit width. At width 1 the question
degenerates (one zero scratch array makes C^(⊗3) free; checked by `verify.py`). In his §7.4 model as written,
m = 3 and m = 4 never save for programs right at every digit width (argued by hand at m = 3, checked by computer
at m = 4), so a search there that tests each candidate at width 2 or more is a good calibration run.

Remaining obligations: the Lean files are not run by the hub's intake (built on an 8-core Linux machine, 11
minutes, 10.06 GB peak); the m = 4 demand determinant is author evidence (C, about an hour); the hand arguments have
AI reviewers only; whether #288's full register model lies inside the engine game is not checked, so #288's open
m = 3 cases are claimed excluded only in the engine game.

## Task and overlap

- Base `f626db5c3a3d781d8f7695038776c621651f75e1`. Card `scope-navigation` (method "Index one tightly related family
  of obstructions with explicit excluded and open hypotheses"), `scope_status: changed`, reason in `TASK.json`: the
  package also adds bounds that are not on main.
- No live inputs from this repository. Provenance rows: the task catalogue, #288's retained README and #2108's
  README. The data files are copied unchanged from my public repository
  (jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean at `86e575e28ed94890872dcff1bb2621d7ff559cbd`); `verify.py` checks each
  file's sha256 and `SOURCES.json` lists the source paths and Git blobs.
- Nearest work and what this adds: #288 (eumemic: FO lemma, m = 2, 50W/21 at m = 3 with W = 2, s = 5 and W = 3,
  s = 8 open) → a Lean proof on an engine's definitions with scratch and singular mixing, 14W/5 at m = 3, and
  bounds at m ≥ 4; #2108 (jmbarrancoml: a five-call solution needs at least four nonmonomial mixing blocks; "We do not
  settle the five-call problem") → excluded in the engine game; #288's doubled-import bound E + σ ≥ 2W and P1's
  "at least 2W children" row → 2W at every block in every game with bounded free steps (argued by hand); Swapnil
  Jain's P1/P2, cited through #288; bit-side
  parallels #468, #720, #1882, #2167, #825, #203, #2613 (other models; not inputs). README section 2 has one
  "closest prior work; this adds" sentence per item and a short factual paragraph on #288's Fano obstruction. I found no hub
  package with bounds at m ≥ 4 or the no-phase m = 3 bound; that is a search result, not a proof of novelty.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-small-m-lower-bounds --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-small-m-lower-bounds
# = python3 -B research/complex-small-m-lower-bounds/verify.py --part main       (PASS_COMPLEX_SMALL_M_LOWER_BOUNDS_MAIN)
#   python3 -B research/complex-small-m-lower-bounds/verify.py --part controls   (PASS_COMPLEX_SMALL_M_LOWER_BOUNDS_CONTROLS)
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/complex-small-m-lower-bounds
```

Standard library only. On a shallow clone at the base with Python 3.12.13 on an Apple M4 (macOS): `--check-only`
passes; the registered replay passes in about 2.4 seconds of wall time (`verify.py` peaks at about 33 MB, the
runner's whole process tree at about 103 MB) and leaves no files behind;
the commit byte check passes on a local commit; the planner selects only this package; the onboarding tests pass
(26). Not run: `--check-source-history` (it needs full Git history), and Linux x86 (no native code is used).

Evidence inside the check: block-2 and block-3 caps by exact vectors over the Gaussian integers, and attained; the
block-3 demand 224 by a certified 224 × 224 minor and by the rank of the whole 280 × 280 block; two calls in a row at
most 144; the character block of rank at least 28 in two formats by two routines; the eight 28 × 28 blocks of the Lean data
file times the formula matrix equal to the identity mod 65537 (the check Lean's kernel ran); the face certificate of
the no-phase bound, exact over Q(i); the m = 4 arithmetic and the format of its certificate; the width-1 program;
every figure and exclusion in the README tables.

Failure controls (each must be rejected, and is): demand certificate with a repeated row, a composite modulus, a row
inside the hook, a 225 × 225 minor; two-call certificate with a changed and a repeated vector; a cap of 79; the three
corrupted certificates of my repository; one Lean inverse entry plus 1; a face cap of 7; a CNOT claimed to keep the
face span; the width-1 program at width 2; 4 in 11 claimed allowed, 5 in 14 and 2 in 7 claimed excluded.

Not run by this package: the Lean build (statements quoted verbatim in README section 5; axioms `propext`,
`Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`; a negative control rejected; two AI reviewers rebuilt or restated it), and the
m = 4 determinant (`author-evidence/check_m0.c`, determinant 1797789153 modulo 2,147,483,629). No independent human
review.

## Credit

eumemic (#288) for the certificate method and the m = 2 and m = 3 results this builds on; Swapnil Jain (P1, P2);
jmbarrancoml (#2108); aliromman (#468), davidgovea (#720), waynenilsen (#1882, #2167), navinor (#825), huxint (#203)
and thakrarsagar (#2613) for the bit-side parallels; OpenAI for the Lean engine and cost model; Ryan Shea for the Lean
tree the files were built in; David Harvey for the questions of README section 7.

Substantial AI assistance: the programs, checks, proofs, Lean files and texts were written by AI agents (Anthropic
Claude) under my direction. The Lean proofs are checked by Lean's kernel; no independent human review is claimed.
Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

In README (`## Open next questions`) and `TASK.json`. The smallest useful follow-ups: 5 in 14 at m = 3 (decide one
sector of its symmetric sub-game exactly, judged at width 6); 2 in 7 at m = 4 (an exact search with address maps
in the middle and phase letters between calls, or a certificate above 3.5 calls per array); whether #288's full
register model keeps the m = 3 hook (list its free elements and test each); 2 in 5 and 3 in 6 at m = 3 with
neighbouring-column maps free; Lean for complex mixing and for 41W/13; 2 in 7, 2 in 8 and 3 in 9 at m = 5 and 6.
